This lesson has no tray of its own and no lesson-specific action. Nine authored tutor rules at version 0.1.0 in tutor/guidance.ts cover four of the five objectives as a ladder rather than a single prompt per state: orient, notice, connect, prioritize, direct and explain for preoxygenation, then one each for ventilation, the effect-site wait, and treating the mechanism of the pressure fall. They carry cooldowns and an urgency flag, so coached withholds everything that is not about to hurt the patient and unassisted says nothing at all while unpromptedOmissions still records what went unsaid for the debrief. Worked example 0.2.0 is the flagship demonstration linked from the landing page, driving the ordinary controls through the real engine and the real models. Its induction beats moved from 190/195 s to 230/235 s at this version, because at the earlier timing the example secured the airway with 150 seconds of end-tidal reserve and scored partly met on the preoxygenation objective it exists to teach; it now measures 190.6 seconds and the beat at 220 s names both clocks out loud. tests/unit/demonstration.test.ts asserts every narration promise against the engine, including that wait, and tests/integration/anesthesia-routine-induction-runs.test.ts pins the transcripts and the version binding.

No tray of its own: the flowmeter and fresh-gas flow, two syringes, a laryngoscope and the ventilator. Two choices carry the lesson and neither is a drug identity. The first is that the preparation has two halves — the objective asks for at least 95% inspired oxygen AND 10 L/min of fresh gas, because a circle system left at 2 L/min rebreathes nitrogen back at the patient however high the dial reads, and a learner who sets only the dial scores partly met. The second is the order, which the cockpit does not enforce: rocuronium before propofol is accepted exactly as readily as the other way round, and only the debrief reports it. The formulary offers rocuronium at 1.0 and 1.2 mg/kg with no lower option and no reversal, so the trade being made is a faster onset against a block that outlasts the case. The lesson intubates nobody, paralyses nobody, gives no real drug, and predicts no outcome for any person or pregnancy.

The transcripts end at 3,600 ticks, past the scenario's reassessment prompt at 2,400 and past the point where every path that secures an airway has sustained capnography. There is no delivery, no emergence and no neonatal handover in this scenario, and the briefing does not offer one: the slice is the preparation, the induction and the airway, and the run stops because that slice is over rather than because the patient reached a state.

The nine authored tutor rules at version 0.1.0 in tutor/guidance.ts apply here, and the preoxygenation ladder is the one that matters, because in this patient the preparation is the whole margin. It reads the inspired fraction and the recorded boluses, so it speaks before the first drug rather than after, and it is silent on the unassisted setting and suppressed while any alarm is active. No rule names the fresh-gas flow and none names the drug order, which is deliberate on both counts: those are the two decisions the debrief exists to report on, and a prompt that supplied either would remove it. Worked example 0.1.0 is the module's ninth observed-state one, and its preparation beat sets both halves in a single accepted action and says which half gets forgotten. It has no beat that starts the ventilator: measured, the engine begins delivering the moment the tube is placed, so such a beat is unreachable and its narration would promise an action no viewer ever sees. One was written and cut, and what it had to say — that placement is a claim and the sustained capnogram is the evidence for it — is in the closing narration instead.
